item.title: [2.0] A genetically engineered porcine model of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma captures the biological complexity of the human disease.
item.description:
Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is a highly aggressive cancer with limited treatment options and poor patient outcomes. The lack of clinically relevant large animal models hinders the investigation of early disease mechanisms and translational therapeutic strategies. In this study, we present a genetically engineered porcine PDAC model involving pancreas-specific activation of latent KRASG12D alone (KC) or in combination with TP53R167H (KPC), developed in a midipig background. KC pigs predominantly developed progressive acinar-to-ductal metaplasia (ADM), whereas KPC pigs showed accelerated tumour progression, including PanINs, invasive carcinoma, perineural invasion, and early lymphatic dissemination. Histopathological and molecular analyses revealed pronounced intra- and inter-tumour heterogeneity, a complex stromal microenvironment, and expression of key PDAC markers. Tumours exhibited early alterations in oncogenic KRAS signalling, including increased dosage and differential expression of isoforms, together with dysregulation of tumour suppressor networks involving p16 and TP53 family members. Single-cell transcriptomics and flow cytometric analyses demonstrated an organised and functionally active immune landscape in early lesions, characterised by infiltrating effector and regulatory T-cell populations. Porcine pancreatic cancer cell lines (PoPaCa) were established from KC and KPC tumours, recapitulating key genetic and transcriptional features of the primary lesions. Exploratory drug screening demonstrated heterogeneous responses to clinically relevant and experimental compounds. Responses to gemcitabine and paclitaxel overlapped qualitatively with those observed in human PDAC cell lines, whereas pronounced sensitivity to the GPX4 inhibitor RSL3 and partial responsiveness to trametinib identified testable therapeutic phenotypes for further validation. Together, this genetically engineered porcine PDAC model captures early molecular, cellular, and microenvironmental features of pancreatic tumorigenesis and provides a translational platform to study disease initiation, tumour heterogeneity, immune interactions, and therapeutic response beyond the constraints of rodent models.
— Source: bioRxiv Subject Collection: Cancer Biology

item.title: [1.8] FasL blockade suppresses liver metastasis and prolongs survival in small-cell lung cancer
item.description:
Small-cell lung cancer (SCLC) is an aggressive malignancy characterised by early metastatic dissemination, frequent relapse and poor long-term survival. Despite advances in immunotherapy, durable disease control remains challenging, highlighting the need to identify therapeutic vulnerabilities beyond conventional tumour-cell killing and immune checkpoint inhibition. Here, we uncover an unexpected contribution of Fas-Fas ligand (FasL) signalling to SCLC metastatic progression and demonstrate the therapeutic potential of targeting this pathway. Using an autochthonous Rb1/Trp53-deficient mouse model, we show that genetic Fas deletion markedly suppresses liver metastatic disease, identifying a previously unrecognised contribution of Fas signalling to metastatic progression. Notably, despite this antimetastatic effect, Fas deletion during tumour initiation did not improve survival and was accompanied by pronounced alterations in pulmonary tissue architecture. As these alterations may reflect adverse consequences of Fas deletion in non-malignant pulmonary populations, we reasoned that pharmacological FasL blockade in established disease could provide therapeutic benefit while circumventing the detrimental consequences for pulmonary tissue homeostasis associated with genetic Fas deletion. Remarkably, only six administrations of a soluble Fas-Fc fusion protein over three weeks significantly prolonged survival and substantially reduced the incidence and burden of liver metastases. FasL blockade was also associated with enhanced inflammatory and immune-response transcriptional signatures in the liver, while its combination with anti-PD-1 increased pulmonary immune-cell accumulation without conferring additional survival benefit. These data suggest that the biological consequences of targeting this pathway may depend on the timing and cellular context of intervention. Together, our findings identify Fas-FasL signalling as an unexpected regulator of SCLC metastatic progression and establish FasL blockade as a promising therapeutic strategy capable of prolonging survival in established disease beyond conventional immune checkpoint inhibition.
— Source: bioRxiv Subject Collection: Cancer Biology

item.title: [2.0] From Calcium-dependent currents to Multitarget Therapy: A Pharmacological Strategy for Glioblastoma
item.description:
Glioblastoma (GBM) is an aggressive primary brain tumor with limited treatment options and substantial interpatient heterogeneity. Ion transport and cell-volume regulation may represent pharmacological vulnerabilities in glioma stem cells (GSCs). Here, we characterized membrane currents in patient-derived GSCs, identifying a calcium-dependent anion conductance consistent with volume-regulated anion channels (VRACs) and an inward current consistent with Na+/Ca++ exchanger exchanger (NCX) activity. Based on these findings, we investigated individual compounds and developed a multitarget cocktail comprising niflumic acid (NFA), bumetanide (BTN), and R-ketorolac (R-K) to target complementary mechanisms involved in ion homeostasis, cell-volume regulation, and cellular dynamics. The cocktail affected cell viability and mechanical properties and showed synergistic effects in U87 cells and patient-derived GSCs with similar electrophysiological profiles. Treatment did not measurably alter spontaneous activity in cultured hippocampal neurons but caused substantial HMC3 cytotoxicity. Encapsulation in transferrin-functionalized liposomes attenuated HMC3 toxicity while preserving activity against glioblastoma cells, suggesting a potential strategy to improve treatment selectivity. Further pharmacological studies identified a potential vulnerability associated with NCX activity, although its contribution to cytotoxicity remains unclear. Overall, our findings highlight electrophysiological heterogeneity in patient-derived GSCs and support further investigation of ion transport as a therapeutic target in GBM. Combining multitarget pharmacology with targeted drug delivery may help address heterogeneous treatment responses, although further studies are needed to establish the underlying mechanisms, safety, and vivo efficacy.
— Source: bioRxiv Subject Collection: Cancer Biology

item.title: [2.1] Focused ultrasound-enhanced carboplatin delivery improves radiotherapy response and survival in a preclinical glioblastoma model
item.description:
Rationale Glioblastoma is highly resistant to conventional therapies due to the limited penetration of chemotherapeutics across the blood-brain and blood-tumor barriers (BBB, BTB). Although platinum-based drugs show strong cytotoxic and radiosensitizing properties in several cancers, their inability to achieve therapeutic concentrations within the central nervous system (CNS) severely limits their efficacy in brain tumors. This study investigated whether focused ultrasound (FUS)-mediated BBB/BTB disruption combined with intravenous carboplatin and stereotactic radiotherapy could improve drug delivery, tumor control, and survival in a preclinical glioblastoma model. Methods F98 glioma-bearing rats were treated with a single dose of 15 Gy radiation therapy (RT), carboplatin only, carboplatin + RT, FUS + carboplatin or FUS + carboplatin + RT. FUS-mediated permeabilization was confirmed by magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and platinum accumulation was quantified by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry and synchrotron X-ray fluorescence. Tumor progression and microenvironmental changes were monitored using multiparametric MRI (diffusion, perfusion, and vascular permeability), followed by voxel-wise clustering analysis and histopathological validation. Results The FUS + carboplatin + RT group demonstrated the strongest therapeutic benefit, compared to all other treatment groups, yielding up to a 122% increase in median survival relative to the untreated group. This treatment also reduced necrotic core expansion and induced a transient increase in tumor perfusion, suggesting improved vascular function. FUS enhanced carboplatin delivery to both the tumor and peritumoral brain, with platinum distribution closely correlating with MRI signal enhancement. Voxel-wise clustering of multiparametric MRI identified biologically distinct tumor regions that were subsequently validated by immunohistochemistry. Conclusion The combination of FUS-mediated carboplatin delivery and radiotherapy represents a safe, non-invasive strategy that enhances drug delivery and improves survival in an aggressive preclinical model of glioblastoma. By overcoming a major limitation of current therapies, this approach shows promising potential for clinical translation. Keywords Glioblastoma, Focused Ultrasound, Blood-Brain Barrier, Chemotherapy, Radiotherapy
— Source: bioRxiv Subject Collection: Cancer Biology

item.title: [1.6] Recurrent astrocyte transcriptional states with spatial and functional specialization are induced by brain metastases independently of their primary tumor origin
item.description:
Reactive astrocytes have emerged as important components of the brain metastasis niche, yet a state-resolved framework for metastasis-associated astrocyte biology is still lacking. Here, we integrate single-cell and spatial transcriptomics across syngeneic breast, lung and melanoma models of brain metastases to define a state-resolved astrocyte landscape. We identify recurrent tumor-associated astrocyte states shared across tumor origins, map their spatial distribution, and find that a subset, which we term AST-BrM, becomes selectively reprogrammed at the tumor-microenvironment interface, supporting niche-coupled organization rather than a diffuse brain-wide reactive response. AST-BrM defines distinct metastasis-associated astrocyte states at the peritumoral interface, distinguishes them from homeostatic-like astrocytes beyond generic inflammatory activation, and resolves into two therapeutically actionable programs: an AP-1-high axis and a STAT3+/HOPX+-associated axis. Genetic and pharmacologicall perturbations establish functional relevance, and an AP-1/c-FOS-driven signature is associated with clinical outcome. Together, these findings define conserved, spatially organized and actionable astrocyte programs that drive brain metastasis progression.
— Source: bioRxiv Subject Collection: Cancer Biology

item.title: [1.7] Combining inhaled hyperoxia and olaparib for treating lung metastases in uveal and cutaneous melanoma
item.description:
Uveal melanoma is highly metastatic, particularly to the liver and lungs, and is frequently associated with loss on chromosome 3 and a gain on chromosome 8. This alteration promotes sustained tumor hypoxia, making this cancer type a strong candidate for reoxygenation strategies aimed at limiting tumor adaptation to hypoxia. Here, we investigated the therapeutic potential of supplemental oxygen, alone or in combination with the PARP inhibitor olaparib which has also been shown to impair tumor adaptation to hypoxia and the would attenuates hyperoxia-induced inflammatory burst, in uveal melanoma cell lines. Non-tumoural lung epithelial cells served as control. Exposure to supplemental oxygen increased oxidative stress and impaired uveal melanoma cell viability, proliferation, and migration, while control cells were minimally affected. Co-treatment with olaparib effectively modulates the hyperoxia-induced inflammatory response. Notably, both hyperoxia and the combination treatment triggered pyroptosis, an immunogenic form of cell death. In vivo, a partial model of metastatic cutaneous melanoma exposed to inhaled hyperoxia showed a significant reduction in lung metastatic burden. These findings support the use of reoxygenation combined with PARP1 inhibitors as a promising strategy to enhance tumor stress responses and promote immunogenic cell death in metastatic uveal melanoma, with an emphasis on the modulation of inflammatory signaling.
— Source: Cancer : nature.com subject feeds

item.title: [1.9] Matrix stiffness drives early OSCC metastasis by inducing a PERK-dependent unfolded protein response
item.description:
Occult metastasis remains a major cause of treatment failure in early-stage oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC). The underlying drivers of this early metastatic switch are poorly understood. Here, through integrated multi-omics analysis of early-stage OSCC, we identify a profound proteostatic crisis, characterized by a severe decoupling of the transcriptome and proteome, as a hallmark of metastatic tumors. This imbalance is driven by heightened endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress, which is orchestrated by the stiff microenvironment enriched with cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) and dense collagen. Mechanistically, we demonstrate that matrix stiffness activates the PERK-associated unfolded protein response (UPR), which not only helps cancer cells survive proteotoxic stress but also promotes a pro-metastatic phenotype. In vitro and in vivo, pharmacologically targeting the ER stress sensor PERK robustly suppressed stiffness-induced invasion and metastasis. Our findings reveal that the matrix stiffness-PERK axis is a critical driver of early OSCC metastasis, offering PERK as a promising therapeutic target.
— Source: Cancer : nature.com subject feeds

item.title: [1.5] Interpretable distance-resolved graph learning for cancer gene priority screening
item.description:
Systematic screening for cancer genes (CGs) is still a central goal in precision oncology, yet integrating sparse and spatially dispersed oncogenic signals to identify testable candidates remains challenging. Here we present CGMap, an interpretable graph-learning framework that uses a width-oriented parallel architecture to prioritize potential CGs from biomolecular networks and trace mechanistic cues. By constructing distance-resolved channels, CGMap localizes spatially dispersed CG signals across multiple topological scales while avoiding representation homogenization. A global diffusion module quantifies gene cooperativity along pathway contexts and yields traceable virtual interactions that map predictions to potential regulatory hypotheses, providing intrinsic interpretability for model decisions. Across multiple biomolecular networks in a pan-cancer setting, CGMap analysed 12,022 genes, consistently outperformed existing methods while remaining computationally efficient and prioritized 70 reliable candidates, including those previously unannotated in established databases. Importantly, the prioritized candidates were associated with the suppression of tumour-related phenotypes, including reduced cell proliferation, migration and invasion, along with a shift of epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT)-related features toward a non-mesenchymal state, as supported by parallel loss-of-function assays across cancer and non-malignant cell lines. Wang et al. propose CGMap, a distance-resolved graph-learning framework that maps dispersed oncogenic signals into structured priorities, narrowing the cancer gene candidate space and establishing an interpretable path from hypotheses to practical validation.
— Source: Cancer : nature.com subject feeds

item.title: [1.5] Development of Novel NPC1-Targeting Autophagy Inhibitors for the Treatment of Uveal Melanoma
item.description:
Background: Uveal melanoma (UM) is the most common primary intraocular malignancy in adults, and up to 50% of patients develop liver metastases. Metastatic UM responds poorly to conventional chemotherapy and currently available immunotherapies, highlighting the need for new therapeutic strategies. Because UM cells rely on lysosome-dependent stress-response pathways, including autophagy, we evaluated previously reported betulinic acid (BetA) derivatives and identified ALS-997 as a potent inhibitor of autophagic flux in UM cells. Methods: The anticancer activity of BetA derivatives was evaluated using the NCI-60 cancer cell line panel and WST-1 viability assays in UM cell lines and normal human melanocytes. Effects on autophagy and lysosomal function were assessed by western blotting for mTOR and autophagy associated proteins, LysoTracker Green imaging, and filipin III/LAMP2 staining. Apoptosis was evaluated by PARP cleavage and caspase-3 cleavage. The interaction of ALS-997 with Niemann-Pick disease type C1 (NPC1) was examined using a cellular thermal shift assay and computational molecular docking. NPC1 expression in UM cells and normal melanocytes was compared by quatitative PCR and western blotting. Results: ALS-997 preferentially reduced the viability of UM cell relative to normal melanocytes. Treatment with ALS-997 disrupted autophagic flux and lysosomal function, induced lysosomal cholesterol accumulation, and activated apoptotic signaling. ALS-997 also altered the thermal stability of NPC1, supporting cellular target engagement, while molecular docking predicted a direct interaction between ALS-997 and NPC1. NPC1 expression was higher in UM cells than in normal melanocytes. Conclusions: ALS-997 is a BetA-derived compound that disrupts lysosomal cholesterol homeostasis and autophagic flux, leading to apoptosis in UM cells. These findings support NPC1 as a potential therapeutic target in UM.
— Source: bioRxiv Subject Collection: Cancer Biology

item.title: [2.3] SLC25A39 loss disrupts mitochondrial redox homeostasis and exposes therapeutic vulnerabilities in glioblastoma
item.description:
Glioblastoma is an incurable brain tumour characterised by extensive hypoxia and phenotypic plasticity, both of which drive therapy resistance. Mitochondrial glutathione, dependent on the inner membrane carrier SLC25A39, is central to buffering the oxidative stress that hypoxia generates; its regulation and significance in glioblastoma are nonetheless unknown. We find that SLC25A39 expression is hypoxia-inducible and HIF-dependent, enriched in hypoxic tumour niches and heterogeneously expressed within and between tumours. Its loss depletes mitochondrial glutathione, causing oxidative damage to nucleic acids and lipids, mitochondrial hyperfusion, impaired respiration and a compensatory shift towards glycolysis, glutamine catabolism and serine synthesis. SLC25A39-deficient cells grow poorly, yet resist temozolomide while becoming markedly sensitive to navitoclax, an inhibitor of Bcl-2 and Bcl-xL, which increases cell killing when combined with radiation and temozolomide. In this work, we identify SLC25A39 as a metabolic vulnerability and candidate stratification marker in glioblastoma.
— Source: bioRxiv Subject Collection: Cancer Biology

item.title: [1.8] Integrated Organoid CRISPR Screening Reveals NF1 as a Gatekeeper of Cervical Squamous Malignant Transformation
item.description:
Abstract Cervical cancer can progress from high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions driven by persistent human papillomavirus (HPV) infection. Identifying the gatekeepers restraining malignant transformation could reveal strategies to prevent and treat cervical cancer. In this study, we integrated single-cell transcriptomics, CRISPR-Cas9 screening, and organoid modeling to dissect this process. Single-cell analysis of patient samples revealed progressive activation of rat sarcoma virus (RAS) and proliferation programs along epithelial differentiation paths. A focused CRISPR screen in HPV-positive pretumoroids identified neurofibromin 1 (NF1) as the top suppressor of malignant transition. NF1 loss accelerated carcinogenesis in organoids, substantially shortening the experimental interval required for the emergence of malignant phenotypes and recapitulating basal cell expansion, altered differentiation marker expression, and tumorigenicity. Mechanistically, NF1 loss enhanced RAS–mitogen-activated protein kinase and phosphoinositide 3-kinase–protein kinase B signaling, promoted proliferative programs, and remodeled chromatin accessibility at regulatory regions enriched for activator protein 1 motifs. Conversely, NF1 restoration in cancer organoids induced apoptosis and suppressed malignant maintenance. Artificial intelligence–guided modeling was used to design a minimal NF1-derived peptide predicted to interact with RAS GTP-binding protein. The NF1-GAP–mimetic peptide reduced tumor organoid viability and cervical lesion–associated bioluminescence in an HPV16-driven mouse model and was associated with local immune-related changes without marked alterations in selected splenic T-cell populations. Together, these findings establish NF1 as a critical constraint on HPV-associated epithelial evolution and provide a time-compressed organoid model of cervical carcinogenesis, offering proof of concept for NF1-inspired therapeutic interception of RAS-associated signaling. Significance: Single-cell atlas and organoid screening identified NF1 loss as a driver of cervical carcinogenesis, which can be rescued with an AI-designed NF1 mimetic peptide that offers a therapeutic paradigm to intercept tumorigenesis.
— Source: Cancer Research Current Issue

item.title: [2.0] RASA2 Promotes Pancreatic Cancer Metastasis by Activating TGFβ-Dependent Noncanonical Hedgehog Signaling
item.description:
Abstract KRAS mutations are a major driver of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). RASA2, a RAS GTPase-activating protein, modulates KRAS protein levels in wild-type (WT) contexts, suggesting that it could play a potential role in PDAC. In this study, we systematically investigated the biological function and molecular mechanisms of RASA2 in PDAC. Integrative analyses of multiple datasets and clinical samples demonstrated that RASA2 was consistently upregulated in KRAS-mutant PDAC and significantly associated with poor prognosis and metastatic progression. Gain- and loss-of-function studies revealed that RASA2 markedly enhanced PDAC cell migration and invasion in both KRAS-mutant and KRAS-WT models, suggesting that its prometastatic activity is largely independent of KRAS mutational status. Transcriptomic and mechanistic analyses revealed that RASA2 activated GLI1 through a TGFβ2-dependent, noncanonical Hedgehog pathway. Mechanistically, RASA2 interacted with RTF1 to promote H2BK120 ubiquitination at the TGFB2 promoter, thereby enhancing TGFB 2 transcription and activating downstream GLI1 signaling. Pharmacologic inhibition of TGFβ signaling or genetic silencing of GLI1 effectively suppressed RASA2-driven migratory, invasive, and metastatic phenotypes in vitro and in vivo . Collectively, these findings reveal a mechanism by which RASA2-dependent epigenetic and transcriptional reprogramming promotes metastatic progression and nominate the RASA2–TGFβ2–GLI1 axis as a potential therapeutic target in PDAC. Significance: RASA2, preferentially upregulated in KRAS-mutant pancreatic cancer, promotes metastasis through an epigenetically regulated, TGFβ2-induced noncanonical Hedgehog/GLI1 axis, revealing a targetable pathway underlying aggressive tumor progression.
— Source: Cancer Research Current Issue

item.title: [1.8] Microenvironmental Prostaglandin F2α Antagonizes FSP1 in Cancer Cells to Sensitize Tumors to Ferroptosis and Immunotherapy
item.description:
Abstract Induction of ferroptosis is a potential strategy for treating cancer and improving the efficacy of immunotherapy. Ferroptosis is driven by excessive peroxidation of polyunsaturated fatty acid–containing phospholipids, suggesting that microenvironmental lipid metabolites may regulate ferroptotic sensitivity. By integrating single-cell and bulk transcriptomics from immunotherapy cohorts, we identified the prostaglandin (PG) pathway as closely associated with tumor ferroptosis and therapeutic efficacy. Further screening revealed PGF2α as a potent endogenous ferroptosis sensitizer. Mechanistically, microenvironmental PGF2α bound to ferroptosis suppressor protein 1 (FSP1) at alanine 295 (A295) and inhibited its enzymatic activity, leading to lipid peroxidation accumulation upon ferroptotic stimuli. Preclinically, PGF2α supplementation or FSP1 ablation enhanced tumoral ferroptosis, potentiated CD8 + T cell–mediated immunity, and suppressed tumor progression in immunocompetent mice. Moreover, PGF2α improved immunotherapy efficacy across multiple mouse models, including subcutaneous allograft, Braf / Pten -driven spontaneous melanoma, and humanized mouse models. Clinically, a high PGF2α activity–related transcriptomic signature correlated with elevated ferroptosis and improved patient survival. Collectively, these findings establish PGF2α as a proferroptotic metabolite and propose that targeting the PGF2α/FSP1 axis may offer an effective cancer immunotherapeutic strategy. Significance: PGF2α promotes ferroptosis by directly binding and inhibiting FSP1 to enhance lipid peroxidation, which potentiates CD8 + T cell-mediated antitumor immunity and offers an approach for improving cancer immunotherapy.
— Source: Cancer Research Current Issue

item.title: [1.6] Neutrophil Extracellular Trap–Derived DNA Activates the ITGB1/FAK Pathway to Promote Lung Adenocarcinoma Metastasis
item.description:
Abstract Neutrophil extracellular traps (NET) have recently emerged as key modulators of cancer progression and metastasis. However, a more comprehensive understanding of the underlying mechanisms could help identify effective strategies to prevent and treat NET-mediated metastasis. In this study, we observed a marked accumulation of intratumoral NETs in metastatic primary lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD). Tumor cells with elevated CXCL2 expression not only recruited neutrophils via interactions with CXCR2 but also facilitated NET formation. In turn, NET-derived DNA (NET-DNA), through specific DNA motifs, directly bound to the extracellular domain of integrin β1 (ITGB1), thereby activating FAK signaling and promoting invasion and metastasis. NET-DNA was capable of enhancing CXCL2 expression through MAPK–ELK1, thereby establishing a positive feedback loop that maintained continuous neutrophil recruitment and NET formation. In both in vitro and in vivo models, targeting either NETs or ITGB1–FAK signaling significantly inhibited LUAD metastasis. These findings suggest that the CXCL2–NET–ITGB1–FAK signaling axis plays a pivotal role in driving NET-mediated metastasis, which provides a rationale for targeting this signaling pathway to inhibit LUAD metastasis. Significance: Tumor-secreted CXCL2 recruits neutrophils and induces formation of neutrophil extracellular traps that bind to integrin β1 to activate FAK signaling and enhance the metastatic potential of lung cancer.
— Source: Cancer Research Current Issue

item.title: [1.8] Bifunctional Phagocytic Synapse Enhancers Remodel the Tumor Microenvironment to Overcome Immunosuppression
item.description:
Abstract Current immunotherapies often fail in immunologically “cold,” macrophage-rich tumor microenvironments (TME). Multitargeting approaches that modulate innate-adaptive immune activation represent a promising frontier in cancer immunotherapy. In this study, we developed phagocytic synapse enhancers (PSE), a class of modular immune engagers comprising a high-affinity PD-L1 binder coupled to a macrophage-stimulating peptide, tuftsin. PSEs strengthened effector–target cell interactions and enhanced tumor phagocytosis by bridging tumor PD-L1 to macrophage neuropilin-1, bypassing the classic FcγR-dependent pathways. The PSEs also acted in cis on PD-L1 + macrophages, accelerating the endocytosis and lysosomal compartmentalization of surface PD-L1 and therefore stripping the immunosuppressive checkpoint from the local microenvironment. Beyond physical clearance, the PSEs reprogrammed macrophage phenotype and triggered a robust proinflammatory cytokine and chemokine response. The lead molecule, long PSE, and its half-life–extended variant fused to the albumin-binding domain, ABD- long PSE, showcased superior efficacy than the macrophage enhancer magrolimab in a syngeneic tumor model of colorectal cancer and an orthotopic model of pancreatic cancer. PSE treatment remodeled the TME by inducing phenotypic changes in the lymphoid and myeloid compartments, together with a reduction of tumor-associated macrophages and regulatory T cells. These findings establish PSEs as bifunctional molecules that complement innate and adaptive immune modulation. The bifunctional design offers a versatile approach for next-generation immunotherapies and provides a blueprint for a plug-and-play platform of immune engagers targeting diverse cancer-associated pathways. Significance: Bifunctional immune modulators that simultaneously boost phagocytosis and block immune checkpoints offer a versatile strategy to reprogram the tumor microenvironment and advance next-generation cancer immunotherapy.
— Source: Cancer Research Current Issue

item.title: [1.9] Aberrant O-Glycosylation Induces IL34-Mediated Immune Remodeling and Promotes Pancreatic Cancer Progression
item.description:
Abstract The Tn antigen, a truncated O-glycan, is frequently elevated in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). Multiple therapeutic approaches targeting Tn have been developed, but they have not demonstrated clear efficacy signals in early-phase clinical studies. Improving Tn-targeted strategies in PDAC will require both overcoming the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment and defining pathways by which truncated O-glycans promote growth and immune evasion. In this study, we show that Tn reshapes the tumor immune landscape of PDAC. Expression of Tn antigen on PDAC cells enhanced proliferation in vitro and tumor growth in vivo . Tn expression remodeled the immune microenvironment, skewing tumor-associated macrophages toward M2-like phenotypes, reducing cross-presenting dendritic cells, and expanding myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSC). Single-cell RNA sequencing confirmed the expansion of MDSCs and downregulation of antigen processing and presentation in the immune cell infiltrate of Tn + tumors. Tumor-intrinsic transcriptomic analyses revealed the activation of TNFα/NF-κB signaling and induction of IL34, a cytokine linked to monocyte survival and differentiation in Tn antigen–expressing tumors. Additionally, high Tn expression in both organoids derived from patients with pancreatic cancer and in PDAC mouse models was associated with increased IL34 expression. The genetic deletion of Il34 in PDAC cells attenuated Tn-driven tumorigenesis and reduced MDSC infiltration, whereas recombinant IL34 promoted myeloid cell differentiation and proliferation in vitro . Together, these findings establish a glyco–immune–cytokine axis in which truncated O-glycans contribute to IL34-mediated immunosuppression, providing mechanistic insights and potential therapeutic targets in PDAC. Significance: Altered glycosylation stimulates TNF-α/NF-κB signaling and induces IL-34-mediated accumulation of suppressive myeloid cells in pancreatic cancer, providing a myeloid-mediated mechanism of immunosuppression that could guide the development of therapies targeting glycosylation.
— Source: Cancer Research Current Issue

item.title: [1.7] Aging Rewires Genetic Dependencies in Antitumor T Cells
item.description:
The aged tumor microenvironment can impair antitumor T-cell function, but the molecular regulators that become limiting in this setting remain poorly defined. In a recent issue of Cell , Chen and colleagues harness in vivo CRISPR screening to compare the effects of genetic perturbations in tumor-reactive CD8 + T cells across young and aged hosts. The screen reveals that increased T-cell persistence or an effector-like transcriptional state does not necessarily translate into improved tumor control and identifies Dusp5 and Zfp219 as distinct functional regulators. DUSP5 broadly restrains ERK-dependent proliferation, and its loss improves tumor control in both young and aged mice. ZFP219, by contrast, preferentially limits cytotoxicity in aged hosts; its deletion increases granzyme expression and improves tumor control specifically in the aged setting. Human tumor datasets show that ZNF219 expression in intratumoral CD8 + T cells increases with age and is associated with poorer clinical outcomes. Moreover, Zfp219 loss enhances the response to PD-1 blockade in aged mice, producing complete tumor clearance in a subset of animals and durable protection after rechallenge. Together, these findings show that host age can reshape the functional consequences of T-cell perturbations and reveal age-dependent genetic vulnerabilities with potential therapeutic relevance.
— Source: Cancer Research Current Issue

item.title: [2.1] Detection of Single-Stranded DNA Gaps Reveals a Functional Biomarker of Therapeutic Response
item.description:
Abstract Single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) gaps represent an underappreciated vulnerability that directly shapes therapeutic response in BRCA -deficient models. Current clinical biomarkers remain anchored to the double-strand break–centric model of homologous recombination deficiency, and there are currently no tools available to detect replication-associated gaps in the clinical setting. In this study, we developed a scalable, clinically adaptable assay that enables real-time, drug-free detection of gaps. This assay demonstrated that gaps are intrinsically elevated in BRCA -deficient cells independent of exogenous DNA damage. These gaps arose during DNA replication and were generated through PRIMPOL-dependent repriming at abasic sites and nuclease-mediated processing. Across diverse cell line models, PARP inhibitor (PARPi) sensitivity was associated with gap burden irrespective of BRCA status, extending the relevance of this vulnerability beyond canonical BRCA-mutant contexts. Integration with artificial intelligence–driven image analysis enabled automated, unbiased quantification of gap levels in xenograft tumor specimens. In BRCA -deficient xenografts, elevated gap levels were associated with PARPi sensitivity, supporting their translational relevance in relation to therapeutic response. Together, these findings establish ssDNA gaps as a real-time functional readout associated with chemotherapy response and introduce an assay with potential for future clinical translation. Significance: Single-stranded DNA gaps are an intrinsic feature of therapy-sensitive cancer cells, representing a functional biomarker that captures replication-associated vulnerabilities.
— Source: Cancer Research Current Issue

item.title: [1.9] YAP1-Driven PLCβ1 Impairs MHC-I Antigen Presentation and Limits Antitumor Immunity in Gastrointestinal Cancer
item.description:
Abstract Immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) has revolutionized cancer treatment, yet its efficacy in gastrointestinal malignancies is often limited by an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. In this study, we identified phospholipase C beta 1 (PLCβ1) as a central driver of pathogenesis and ICB resistance in gastrointestinal cancer. Unlike classical oncogenes, PLCβ1 promoted tumor progression by fostering immune evasion rather than directly enhancing intrinsic tumor cell survival. Mechanistically, PLCβ1 interacted with ERC1, promoting its ubiquitin–proteasomal degradation. ERC1 destabilization suppressed NF-κB–dependent transcriptional activation of MHC-I, thereby impairing antigen presentation. Upstream, the YAP1 complex served as a direct transcriptional activator of PLCβ1, and pharmacologic disruption of this pathway using the YAP inhibitor effectively restored MHC-I expression. Expression of PLCβ1 was associated with reduced responsiveness to immunotherapy in patients, and combining the YAP inhibitor with anti–PD-1 therapy elicited synergistic antitumor responses in both syngeneic mice and patient-derived xenografts. Collectively, these findings uncover the YAP1–PLCβ1–MHC-I axis as a critical mechanism of immune escape and propose combinatorial YAP inhibition as a promising strategy to sensitize gastrointestinal tumors to immunotherapy. Significance: PLCβ1 is a critical determinant of tumor immunogenicity in gastrointestinal malignancies by suppressing MHC-I expression and antigen presentation, providing rationale for targeting this axis to overcome immunotherapy resistance.
— Source: Cancer Research Current Issue

item.title: [1.7] Cytotoxic drugs and bispecific T cell engagers synergize to rewire host immunity and elicit polyclonal antitumor T cell responses
item.description:
Cytotoxic therapies such as chemotherapy and antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) kill tumor cells directly but are limited by resistance, dose-limiting toxicity, and failure to induce durable antitumor immunity. Here we show that tumor-associated antigen (TAA)-targeted CD28 bispecific antibodies (TAAxCD28) convert cytotoxic agents into drivers of durable antitumor immunity. In humanized mouse models, combining the HER2-directed ADC trastuzumab deruxtecan (Tras-DXd) with TAAxCD28 antibodies enhances tumor rejection and promotes durable immune memory in Tras-DXd-resistant cancers, and comparable synergy is observed with 5-fluorouracil (5-FU). This therapeutic strategy allows lower or less frequent cytotoxic drug dosing, potentially limiting systemic toxicity. Mechanistically, TAAxCD28 antibodies promote the activation and expansion of clonally-restricted tumor CD8+ T cells, and adding ADCs or chemotherapy sustains this activation while preserving a naïve/stem-like pool of tumor-specific CD8+ T cells with a diversified T cell receptor repertoire. Each cytotoxic agent supports this T cell activity through a separate innate mechanism: Tras-DXd expands and activates conventional dendritic cells, whereas 5-FU reprograms suppressive myeloid cells toward an immunostimulatory phenotype. Together, these findings support pairing cytotoxic agents with TAAxCD28 bispecifics to overcome resistance and improve long-term tumor control in refractory cancers. TAA×CD28 costimulatory bispecific antibodies are a class of immunotherapeutics that provide tumor-targeted CD28 costimulation to T cells by crosslinking CD28 on T cells to a tumor-associated antigen (TAA) expressed on tumor cells. Here, the authors show that cytotoxic therapies reprogram the tumor microenvironment and augment the antitumor immunity induced by TAA×CD28 bispecifics.
— Source: Cancer : nature.com subject feeds

item.title: [1.6] SRSF3-mediated post-transcriptional regulation of SERPINH1 promotes tumor growth and immune evasion in hepatocellular carcinoma
item.description:
Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is characterized by aggressive progression and a profoundly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). Serine/arginine-rich splicing factor 3 (SRSF3) is a key regulator of alternative splicing, yet its role in shaping the immune microenvironment and fibrotic remodeling in HCC remains poorly understood. SRSF3 expression was examined in human HCC tissues and cell lines by immunohistochemistry, qPCR, and Western blot. Gain- and loss-of-function approaches were used to evaluate the effects of SRSF3 on HCC cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and cytokine secretion in vitro. RNA immunoprecipitation was performed to assess the interaction between SRSF3 and SERPINH1 mRNA. Tumor growth, immune cell infiltration, and fibrosis were analyzed in mouse tumor models with SRSF3 manipulation or overexpression of distinct SERPINH1 isoforms using flow cytometry, histology, and immunofluorescence. SRSF3 was markedly upregulated in HCC tissues and correlated with poor prognosis, reduced cytotoxic immune infiltration, increased regulatory T cells, and elevated PD-L1 expression. Functionally, SRSF3 promoted HCC cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and secretion of immunosuppressive cytokines. In vivo, SRSF3 accelerated tumor growth and reshaped the TME toward an immunosuppressive phenotype. Mechanistically, SRSF3 directly bound to SERPINH1 mRNA and enhanced its expression. Among SERPINH1 isoforms, the short isoform exerted the strongest pro-tumorigenic and pro-fibrotic effects, promoting collagen deposition, tumor proliferation, and immune exclusion. Our findings identify SRSF3 as a critical driver of HCC progression by orchestrating tumor growth, fibrosis, and immune evasion through regulation of SERPINH1, particularly its short isoform. Targeting the SRSF3–SERPINH1 axis may represent a promising strategy to simultaneously inhibit tumor progression and improve antitumor immune responses in HCC.
— Source: Cancer : nature.com subject feeds

item.title: [1.7] GKB202 suppresses malignant phenotypes of circulating tumor cells in non-small cell lung cancer by modulating adaptive oxidative stress responses
item.description:
Antrodia cinnamomea is a Taiwan-endemic medicinal fungus with reported anti-inflammatory and anticancer activities. Circulating tumor cells (CTCs) contribute to metastasis and therapy resistance in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). This study investigated whether stress-adaptive programs supporting CTC survival can be pharmacologically disrupted by GKB202, a purified derivative of A. cinnamomea. Patient-derived NSCLC CTCs were isolated and treated with GKB202 followed by RNA sequencing. Differential expression, pathway enrichment, and rank-rank hypergeometric overlap (RRHO) analyses were performed using a public NSCLC bone metastasis dataset (GSE175601). Functional assays in A549 cells assessed proliferation, migration, and invasion. MT1E protein expression was examined by Western blotting, and metabolomic profiling was conducted using UPLC-QTOF/MS. Untreated CTCs showed enrichment of migration- and lipid metabolism-related programs, whereas GKB202 treatment was associated with enrichment of stress-adaptive and detoxification pathways. Metallothionein-1E (MT1E) expression increased following GKB202 treatment. GKB202 reduced CTC viability and its combination with cisplatin produced a greater reduction in viability than either treatment alone in patient-derived CTC cultures. In A549 cells, GKB202 reduced proliferation and migration, accompanied with time-dependent changes in MT1E protein expression. Exploratory metabolomic profiling showed alterations in lipid-associated metabolic pathways consistent with stress-responsive regulation. These findings suggest that GKB202 is associated with changes in stress-adaptive molecular and metabolic programs in NSCLC models, together with reductions in selected malignant phenotypes and modulation of MT1E-associated responses. By potentially modulating compensatory stress responses in CTCs, GKB202 may increase their vulnerability to therapeutic stress, a possibility that warrants further investigation in the context of CTC-associated metastatic progression in NSCLC.
— Source: Cancer : nature.com subject feeds

item.title: [1.7] Minor intron splicing restricts E2F transcription factor activity in RB-deregulated prostate cancer
item.description:
Castration-resistant prostate cancer with neuroendocrine differentiation (CRPC-NE) arises in RB1-mutated lineage plastic cells in response to androgen receptor (AR)-targeted therapies. RB1 loss leads to constitutive E2F activation and cylin-dependent kinase (CDK) inhibitor resistance, making it challenging to restrict E2F activity. A post-transcriptional node is that typical E2Fs contain a rare but highly conserved minor intron, processed by the minor spliceosome (MiS). In an in vivo CRISPR screen, we nominate the MiS as the strongest dependency, and U6atac correlates strongest with E2F transcriptional programs in a clinical CRPC cohort. U6atac depletion led to mis-splicing of typical E2Fs, cell cycle arrest, and translation of a minor intron-containing E2F1 isoform (E2F1-MIRI) as a pharmacodynamic biomarker. Combined E2F activator depletion, induced further neuroendocrine (NE) specification. U6atac depletion shifted NE identity along the ASCL1 axis without the secretory granule program, and induced cell-surface antigens including DLL3, nominating MiS inhibition as a combination partner for antigen-directed agents.
— Source: bioRxiv Subject Collection: Cancer Biology

item.title: [2.1] Identifying potential combinatorial mechanism between paclitaxel and Almonertinib in lung cancer through multi-omics integration
item.description:
Combination therapy using epidermal growth factor receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitors (EGFR-TKIs) and cytotoxic chemotherapy is a promising strategy to overcome resistance in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, the complicated molecular mechanisms remain elusive. Here, we employed an integrated multi-omics approach to dissect the molecular responses to the third-generation EGFR-TKI Almonertinib (Alm) and paclitaxel (PTX) and their combination in EGFR-mutant NSCLC cells. Transcriptomic and metabolomic profiling revealed that the combination therapy elicits an unique molecular signature distinct from either monotherapy alone. We identified a specific gene cluster (C8) that was suppressed only by the drug combination, and mainly enriched in cell cycle, DNA replication and mitochondrial function. The downregulation of these processes was validated in H1975 cells, and key genes (e.g., XRCC2, SKA3, TOMM40) also exhibited prognostic relevance. Meanwhile, metabolomic analysis uncovered a combination-specific blockade of mitochondrial fatty acid oxidation, evidenced by L-Carnitine depletion and accumulation of Hexanoyl-L-Carnitine and Oleoyl-L-Carnitine. This work demonstrates the potential combination interaction of Alm and PTX, converging on the suppression of cell cycle and the induction of carnitine metabolism blockage. Our findings provide a profound mechanistic rationale for this combination therapy.
— Source: Cancer : nature.com subject feeds

item.title: [2.0] Discovery of molecular glues for modulating MHC presentation of cancer neoantigens
item.description:
Antigen presentation by MHC class I molecules is essential for cancer immunosurveillance, but many cancer-specific antigens fail to form complexes with Class I MHC and are poorly presented on the cell surface. In this study, we present a chemical strategy to overcome this limitation by identifying peptide MHC glues (PMGs) that promote the formation of peptide-MHC complexes with otherwise unpresentable cancer antigens. Crystal structures of these complexes show that our compounds stabilize antigen-MHC binding by making simultaneous interactions with the MHC protein and the antigen peptides. These findings reveal a new approach for chemically rewiring Class I MHC antigen presentation and accessing rare cancer antigens for therapeutic targeting.
— Source: bioRxiv Subject Collection: Cancer Biology

item.title: [1.6] Author Correction: The conformation-selective PI3Kδ inhibitor roginolisib in patients with advanced or metastatic cancer, including metastatic uveal melanoma: first-in-human clinical trial
item.description: — Source: Cancer : nature.com subject feeds

item.title: [1.5] Diffuse assemblies drive oncogenic signalling
item.description:
Cytoplasmic condensates formed by receptor tyrosine kinase (RTK) fusion oncoproteins have been implicated in the regulation of oncogenic signalling. A study shows that low‑order RTK assemblies operate independently of condensate formation and that they are sufficient to activate the canonical RAS–ERK cascade driving downstream oncogenic output.
— Source: Cancer : nature.com subject feeds

item.title: [2.2] Low-order assemblies drive oncogenic RTK fusion signalling without condensation
item.description:
Receptor tyrosine kinase (RTK) fusions are a large class of oncoproteins found in ~5% of cancers. Key questions remain, however, about how RTK fusions transmit oncogenic signals, including how these largely cytoplasmic proteins activate downstream pathways that originate at the plasma membrane. Fusions are often multimeric and can form mesoscale condensates in cancer cells, and condensation has been implicated as an essential mechanism to enable signal transmission from the cytoplasm. However, whether condensates play a causal role or whether smaller ‘diffuse’ assemblies are sufficient to transduce signals, has been challenging to establish. Here we apply advanced microscopy, single-cell analysis and synthetic fusions to determine the principles by which multimerization and condensation drive signalling from cytoplasmic RTK fusions. For EML4–ALK, a prominent fusion that forms condensates, we found poor correlation between condensation and signalling and abundant EML4–ALK activity in the diffuse phase. Synthetic RTK fusions showed that cytoplasmic dimers of ALK or RET domains—and even constitutively active monomers—were sufficient to induce strong Ras–Erk signalling despite the absence of condensates, and non-condensing fusions were sufficient to transform cells in vitro and in subcutaneous tumour models. A panel of various other cancer-driving RTK fusions showed that low-order multimerization was widespread across fusions, whereas mesoscale condensation was rare and did not correlate with signalling. Our results suggest that low-order multimerization is sufficient to drive fusion phosphorylation, which is necessary and sufficient to trigger downstream oncogenic signalling. Gonzalez-Martinez, Mumford et al. show that condensate-forming fusion oncoprotein EML4–ALK can drive oncogenic Ras–Erk signalling from small multimers in the dilute phase, whereas its propensity for biomolecular condensation is dispensable.
— Source: Cancer : nature.com subject feeds

item.title: [2.0] NRF2-driven thiol metabolism creates a selective vulnerability to selenite
item.description:
NRF2 hyperactivation caused by mutations in KEAP1 or NFE2L2 occurs in 20-30% of non-small cell lung cancers and confers therapy resistance. Here we show that NRF2-driven metabolic reprogramming creates a selective vulnerability to selenite. NRF2-dependent thiol export promotes the extracellular reduction of selenite to selenide. Our data support a model in which selenide enters cells and reaches mitochondria, where sulfide-quinone oxidoreductase uses selenide and glutathione to generate the selenopersulfide GS-SeH. A four-hour pulse of selenite was sufficient to induce cell death after washout, consistent with a selenium redox cycle that consumes NADPH and regenerates selenide. Within hours, selenite abolished aconitase activity and impaired mitochondrial respiration. The resulting cell death occurred independently of apoptosis, ferroptosis, pyroptosis, necroptosis and disulfidptosis. In mice, a selenite-rich diet selectively suppressed the growth of NRF2-hyperactive tumors. These findings identify an NRF2-driven metabolic vulnerability and support further investigation of selenite as a therapeutic strategy for NRF2-hyperactive cancers.
— Source: bioRxiv Subject Collection: Cancer Biology

item.title: [1.6] Multimodal Liquid Biopsy Improves Longitudinal Circulating Tumor DNA Detection in Children with Central Nervous System Tumors
item.description:
Background: Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) is a promising biomarker for pediatric central nervous system (CNS) tumors, but limitations in sensitivity and universally accepted detection criteria remain. We evaluated multimodal ctDNA detection using a novel composite scoring framework integrating mutation, copy number, and fragmentomic analysis in longitudinal plasma and CSF samples from children with CNS tumors. Methods: Tumor, blood and/or CSF samples were collected from pediatric CNS tumor patients. DNA was extracted from plasma, CSF, tumor, and whole blood. All samples underwent targeted and whole genome sequencing. Plasma and CSF samples were evaluated for ctDNA positivity--defined by a composite score [≥]2--utilizing a tri-modal approach of whole genome sequencing for copy number alterations and fragmentomics and targeted sequencing. Results: The cohort included 28 patients: medulloblastoma (39%), diffuse midline glioma (25%), high-grade glioma (18%), pilocytic astrocytoma (11%), and ependymoma (7%). A total of 140 plasma and 27 CSF samples were collected longitudinally. Combining all three modalities identified ctDNA in 70% of CSF and 17% of plasma samples, exceeding rates achieved by any single modality alone. Post-diagnosis plasma ctDNA positivity was significantly associated with worse progression-free and overall survival. CSF demonstrated significantly higher ctDNA signal intensity than plasma across all assay modalities. Conclusions: A multimodal composite scoring approach improves longitudinal ctDNA detection in pediatric CNS tumors. Although CSF remains the most sensitive biofluid, plasma ctDNA reflects disease progression in select patients. These findings support integrated, multimodal liquid biopsy strategies for disease monitoring and highlight the need for prospective validation of standardized detection criteria.
